name: Stuart Bruce
title: Digital PR strategist, crisis communications consultant and public affairs specialist
bio_short: Digital PR strategist listed in PRWeek's Power Book. Fellow of both CIPR and AMEC. Clients include Google, Rolls-Royce, Bank of England and the UK Cabinet Office. Davos World Communication Forum Executive Committee member. 30-year career.
bio: Stuart is a digital PR strategist and crisis communications consultant who is listed in PRWeek's Power Book of the UK's most influential public relations professionals. He has advised and trained clients in more than 40 countries, including Google, Rolls-Royce, the UK Cabinet Office, the Bank of England, Total, Frontex, the Office of the President of the European Parliament, KAUST, DuPont, the NHS and the Metropolitan Police.  Stuart is a Chartered PR Practitioner and one of only seven fellows of the International Association for the Measurement and Evaluation of Communications (AMEC) globally. He is also a Fellow of the Chartered Institute of Public Relations (CIPR) and a member of the Executive Committee of the World Communication Forum Association in Davos. He is a visiting lecturer at Rotterdam School of Management at Erasmus University and Leeds Beckett University, and co-author of the CIPR handbooks Share This and Share This Too.  At ISOC, Stuart delivers digital PR, social media, corporate communications, crisis communication, AI communications and measurement programmes. His 30-year career includes co-founding one of the UK's first digital PR agencies, in-house roles at Grant Thornton and the Labour Party, and a decade as an international adviser and trainer. Stuart is based in the UK and trains in English.

He was awarded the Outstanding Contribution to Social Media Award in 2013.  At ISOC, Stuart delivers digital PR, social media, corporate communications, crisis communication, AI communications and measurement programmes. His 30-year career includes co-founding one of the UK's first digital PR agencies, growing it within two years to a PRWeek Top 150 Consultancy, in-house roles at Grant Thornton and the Labour Party, and a decade as an international adviser and trainer. He regularly comments on communications trends for Al Jazeera and France 24. Stuart is based in the UK and trains in English.
